Wiki → Confluence — publish articles to a Confluence space

Publish a Wiki article's published version to a Confluence space, one way, as a page SATOM keeps updating; spaces are set up by Wiki moderators, the credential stays in the vault, and a credential scan and an audience check run before anything leaves.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionswiki.write wiki.moderate
📍 WhereWiki → Confluence (moderators, URL /wiki/confluence) and the Confluence block of an article

What is it?#

A Wiki article can be published to Confluence, one way: SATOM writes the page, Confluence never writes back, and the page is replaced each time the article is published there again. The page's last line says so and links back to the article in SATOM. Confluence Cloud (REST API v2) and Confluence Data Center / Server are supported.

Where is it?#

  • Wiki → Confluence (menu on the left of the Wiki, moderators only): the spaces articles can go to.
  • The Confluence block on an article, shown to its author and the moderators once a space exists.

How to use#

Set up a space (moderator)#

  1. Create the credential in Confluence: on Cloud, an API token for the account that will own the pages (id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens); on Data Center, a personal access token. Give that account permission to add pages in the space.
  2. Open Wiki → Confluence and fill New target:
Field
Confluence Cloud (REST API v2) or Data Center / Server
Address https://<site>.atlassian.net/wiki on Cloud (/wiki is added for an atlassian.net address), or the Data Center base address. https:// only
Space key the space pages are created in
Parent page id optional: new pages go under it (the number in the page's address)
Authentication User + API token (Cloud: the account's e-mail) or Personal access token
API token / password write-only
  1. Save, then Test: it reads the space and shows its name.

Publish an article#

  1. Publish the article in the Wiki first: only a published version goes, never a draft.
  2. On the article, in Confluence, pick the space.
  3. If the article is limited to ADOMs, profiles or groups, tick The readers of that Confluence space may read it: Confluence knows nothing of SATOM's audience.
  4. Press Publish version N. The first time creates a page; later times update that page (by its id) with the next Confluence version, even if its title changed.

The block lists each page, the version it holds and whether it is up to date. Forget stops updating a page and leaves it in Confluence.

Credential check#

Before publishing, the title, description and text are scanned for what looks like a credential: private keys, cloud, Git, Slack, Atlassian and JSON Web tokens, FortiOS set … ENC … secrets, user:password@ in an address, Authorization: headers, and password: …-style values that are not placeholders (<password>, ${VAR}, ****, changeme). Findings are listed by kind and line — never the value — on the article, and they stop the publication. Remove them and publish again. A moderator who has checked that they are not credentials may tick the override; that is audited.

Safety#

  • The credential is kept like every SATOM secret: in the vault when one is configured, otherwise encrypted, and it is never shown again. Changing a space's address, flavour, authentication or user removes it, so an edit can never send a stored credential somewhere new.
  • Calls go through the same checked path as Python Studio connections: no address of the node itself, its HA peer, loopback or link-local; the checked address is the one dialled; redirects are not followed; the credential is removed from every error message.
  • Raw HTML in the article stays text, unsafe links are removed, links to SATOM pages become plain text (they mean nothing in Confluence), and images are linked by their address.
  • Every publication, refusal, Forget and space change is written to the Audit log (wiki.confluence.*).
  • Deleting an article or a space in SATOM leaves its pages in Confluence.

Permissions#

Permission Allows
wiki.write publish your own published articles to an existing space
wiki.moderate set up spaces; publish any article; override a credential warning

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Cause and fix
No Confluence block on the article You are not its author or a moderator, the article is not published, or no space is enabled.
"Confluence refused the credential (HTTP 401)" Wrong e-mail/token pair, an expired token, or a Data Center token used as User + API token. Enter the credential again.
"Space … not found" on Test Wrong space key, or the account cannot see the space.
"A page with this title may already exist in the space" Confluence titles are unique per space. Rename the article or the existing page.
"The article looks like it holds credentials" Remove them (or, for a moderator, override after checking). The message gives kind and line.
"Confluence could not be reached: … refused" The address resolves to this node, its HA peer, loopback or link-local, which SATOM never calls.
"Confluence answered with a redirect to …" Set the space's address to where it points (often /wiki missing).
The credential disappeared after an edit The address, flavour, authentication or user changed: enter it again.
Edits made in Confluence are gone Publishing is one way: the next publication replaces the page. Edit in SATOM.
